children: A number of stocks jumped in the morning session after peer Palo Alto Networks beat fiscal first-quarter 2027 expectations and raised its full-year revenue forecast, lifting shares across the cybersecurity sector.

Palo Alto Networks posted revenue of $3.45 billion, up 39% year over year, non-GAAP diluted net income of $1.05 per share, and 66% growth in next-generation security annual recurring revenue to $9.73 billion, the company's earnings release revealed. Those results beat S&P analyst estimates of $3.31 billion and 97 cents in adjusted earnings per share, CNBC reported, while management's projected fiscal 2027 revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion and non-GAAP diluted net income of $4.26 to $4.30 per share topped consensus forecasts of $14.16 billion and $4.18.

Chairman and CEO Nikesh Arora said in the release that the company delivered a "record Q1" as customers turned to it to protect against an "unprecedented threat environment."When a major vendor pairs higher annual guidance with heightened threat activity, investors often extrapolate steadier enterprise budgets across peers.

The backdrop from the previous session might also have contributed to the momentum after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned in congressional testimony reported by Bloomberg that Iranian-backed actors have targeted U.S. financial, energy, and transportation systems, while CNBC noted recent Microsoft and FAA outages kept security spending in focus.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Cloudflare’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 46 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Cloudflare is up 63.6% since the beginning of the year, but at $320.61 per share, it is still trading 11.2% below its 52-week high of $360.93 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Cloudflare’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,519.
